description: Agavoids explained: rosette-forming, drought-tolerant plants like Agave, Yucca, Nolina and Dasylirion. Growing basics, safety tips and hardiness by zone.
The genus Agave: taxonomy, natural habitats, Gentry's groups and a full species list, plus growing tips for agaves in temperate and Mediterranean climates.
Agave parryi, a variable cold-hardy agave from Arizona to Mexico: subspecies and varieties compared, hardiness, cultivation tips and notable cultivars.
The genus Beaucarnea, home of the ponytail palm: taxonomy, Mexican habitats, cold hardiness by species, indoor and outdoor care, and conservation status.
The genus Beschorneria: spineless, shade-tolerant Mexican agavoids with coral-pink flower stalks. Species list, cold hardiness, cultivation and cultivars.
The genus Calibanus, now in Beaucarnea: boulder-like Mexican caudiciforms. Taxonomy, habitat, cold hardiness, growing tips and both species profiled.
The genus Dasylirion (sotols): 23 species with synonyms, how to tell them from Nolina and Agave, sotol spirit, cold hardiness and growing tips by climate.
The genus Doryanthes, Australia's giant spear lilies: Doryanthes excelsa and D. palmeri compared, habitat, pollination, conservation and growing advice.
The genus Dracaena, from dragon trees to snake plants (ex Sansevieria): taxonomy, species groups, care for tree and rhizomatous types, and conservation.
Dracaena draco, the dragon tree: a spectacular succulent that can be grown outdoors in the most sheltered gardens of mild climates. Origin, growth, care.
The genus Furcraea, agave-like plants of tropical America: naming pitfalls, fique and Mauritius hemp fibers, cold hardiness by species and growing tips.
The genus Hesperaloe (red yucca, false yucca): all 8 species, spineless clumping agavoids with long bloom. Cold hardiness, landscape uses and cultivars.
The genus Hesperoyucca, split from Yucca and closest to Hesperaloe: Our Lord's candle and its kin, the yucca moth, monocarpy, hardiness and growing tips.
The genus Manfreda, now sunk into Agave: soft, spotted, polycarpic agavoids, key species with their Agave names, Mangave hybrids and cultivation advice.
The genus Nolina (beargrasses): tree-forming and stemless species, how to tell them from Dasylirion and Beaucarnea, cold hardiness and a full species list.
The genus Yucca, from Joshua trees to Great Plains yuccas: species grouped by section and series, yucca moth pollination, hardiness and garden choices.
Alooids explained: Aloe, Haworthia, Gasteria and the genera split from Aloe since 2013. Growing tips, intergeneric hybrids and plant choices by USDA zone.
Aloes grow wild in Africa and the Middle East, with Madagascar and South Africa as major centres of diversity. Discover the species and how to grow them.
The genus Aloestrela: Aloestrela suzannae, an unbranched, night-flowering tree aloe from Madagascar. Taxonomy debate, biology, growing and conservation.
The genus Aloiampelos, the climbing and scrambling aloes of southern Africa: all seven species, the cold-hardy A. striatula, cultivation and propagation.
The genus Aloidendron, the tree aloes: the quiver tree and five other species, desert and forest clades, conservation threats and how to grow them.
The genus Aristaloe: the lace aloe, Aristaloe aristata, a haworthioid that only looks like an aloe. Taxonomy, cold hardiness, easy care and propagation.
The genus Astroloba: twelve columnar, star-flowered succulents from the Karoo. Taxonomy, all species, growing in shade and conservation.
The genus Gasteria: shade-loving South African succulents with tongue-shaped leaves. Species by genome group, easy indoor care, propagation and hybrids.
The genus Gonialoe: the tiger aloe Gonialoe variegata and its two Namibian relatives. Taxonomy, rainfall gradient, species profiles and growing advice.
The genus Haworthia and its split into Haworthia, Haworthiopsis and Tulista: windowed and zebra species, indoor care, propagation and collector picks.
The genus Haworthiopsis, home of the zebra plant: 18 hard-leaved species organized by section, how to tell them from Haworthia, easy care and propagation.
The genus Kumara: the fan aloe Kumara plicatilis and the cliff-dwelling K. haemanthifolia. Taxonomy, fynbos habitat and winter-growing care tips.
The genus Tulista: four robust, pearl-studded haworthioids from the Western Cape, including the pearl plant. Identification, species profiles and care.
The Anacardiaceae, or cashew family: classification, distribution, key traits and uses, plus the pachycaulous genera Operculicarya and Pachycormus.
The genus Operculicarya: eight pachycaulous trees from Madagascar, including the bonsai favorite O. decaryi. Habitat, species, care and conservation.
Pachycormus discolor, the elephant tree of Baja California, with its swollen, peeling white trunk and pink flowers. Habitat, morphology and growing tips.
Succulent Apocynaceae: Pachypodium, Adenium, Plumeria, stapeliads, Ceropegia, Hoya and caudiciform climbers. How to tell them apart and shared care rules.
The genus Pachypodium: 25 species from Madagascar and southern Africa, from Madagascar palms to caudex plants. Classification, CITES status and care.
The Burseraceae, or frankincense family: resinous, often pachycaulous trees. Classification, traits and uses, with Commiphora, Bursera and Boswellia.
The genus Boswellia, source of frankincense: about 20 species from Africa, Arabia and India. Papery bark, key species, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Bursera, the elephant trees and copals of Mexico: swollen trunks, colorful peeling bark, copal resin, notable species and how to grow them.
The genus Commiphora, source of myrrh: some 200 pachycaulous species from Africa and Arabia. Peeling bark, notable species, cultivation and conservation.
The cactus family explained: the areole, the six subfamilies of the 2025 classification, key genera, growth forms, adaptations and conservation.
The genus Astrophytum, star cacti of Mexico and Texas: bishop's hat, sand dollar cactus and relatives. Morphology, species, cultivation and CITES status.
Carnegiea gigantea, the saguaro and sole species of its genus: the giant cactus of the Sonoran Desert. Growth, flowers, fruits, cultivation and protection.
The genus Cereus: tall columnar cacti from South America with large night-blooming flowers. Main species like Cereus repandus, care and cold hardiness.
The genus Cleistocactus: slender Andean columnar cacti with tubular, nearly closed flowers loved by hummingbirds, like the silver torch. Species and care.
The genus Echinocactus and its golden barrel cactus: six Mexican barrel species, their morphology, habitat, main species, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Echinopsis, now including Trichocereus: globular and columnar South American cacti with huge flowers. Main species, care and cold hardiness.
The genus Ferocactus, the fierce barrel cacti of Mexico and the Southwest: hooked spines, main species like the fishhook barrel, cultivation and hardiness.
The genus Gymnocalycium: about 80 South American cacti with naked flower buds, source of the colorful moon cactus. Main species and easy care.
The genus Mammillaria, some 200 pincushion cacti with spiraled tubercles and crowns of flowers. Old lady and powder puff cactus, care, hardiness and CITES.
The genus Melocactus, the Turk's cap cacti: globular plants topped by a woolly cephalium. Caribbean and American species, growing needs and conservation.
The genus Myrtillocactus: four candelabra-shaped cacti from Mexico and Guatemala with edible, blueberry-like fruits. Rootstock uses, care and hardiness.
The genus Opuntia, prickly pears and nopales: flat pads, glochids and edible fruits. Main species from Indian fig to bunny ears, care and cold hardiness.
The genus Parodia, now including Notocactus: colorful, free-flowering South American ball cacti. Main species, growing tips and good cold tolerance.
The genus Pilosocereus: blue, waxy columnar cacti with woolly flowering areoles, mainly from Brazil's caatinga. Main species, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Rhipsalis: spineless forest epiphytes, the only cacti also native to the Old World. Mistletoe cactus, key species and care as a houseplant.
The genus Schlumbergera, the Christmas and Thanksgiving cacti: epiphytes from Brazil's Atlantic Forest. Species, how to trigger winter blooms and care.
The genus Selenicereus, now including Hylocereus: climbing cacti with huge night flowers, dragon fruit and the queen of the night. Main species and care.
The genus Stenocereus: columnar cacti of Mexico with edible pitayas, from the organ pipe cactus to the creeping devil. Main species, care and conservation.
Chamaerops, the European fan palm: a monotypic palm genus whose single species, Chamaerops humilis, is the only palm native to continental Europe.
The Crassulaceae, or stonecrop family: some 35 genera and 1,400 species, from jade plants to houseleeks. Classification, all genera, care, pests and uses.
The genus Aeonium: about 40 rosette succulents centered on the Canary Islands. Taxonomy, sections and species, adaptations and popular cultivars.
Aeonium arboreum, the classic tree aeonium from the Canaries and Morocco: subspecies, cultivars such as Zwartkop, winter-growing care and propagation.
The genus Crassula: over 200 species of succulents, mostly from southern Africa. Taxonomy, subgenera and sections, CAM photosynthesis and species list.
Crassula perfoliata, type species of Crassula, and its propeller plant var. falcata: the four varieties, habitat, care, how to get blooms and propagation.
Cycads, the oldest living seed plants: evolution, the ten genera, biology from coralloid roots to heated cones and why 71% of species are threatened.
The genus Bowenia: two Australian cycads with fern-like bipinnate leaves and underground stems. Taxonomy, range, shade-loving cultivation and propagation.
The genus Ceratozamia, the horned cycads of Mexico and Central America: about 35 shade-loving cloud forest species. Species list, CITES status and care.
The genus Cycas: about 120 species from Africa to Asia, Australia and the Pacific, including the sago palm. Hardiness, propagation, pests and species list.
The genus Dioon: about 18 cycads from Mexico and Honduras, drought-tolerant and formal. Discover hardiness, cultivation, propagation and the species list.
The genus Encephalartos: about 68 African cycads, all in CITES Appendix I. Explore conservation, hardiness, cultivation, propagation and species by region.
The genus Lepidozamia: two rainforest cycads from eastern Australia, including Lepidozamia hopei, the tallest living cycad. Cultivation and propagation.
The genus Macrozamia includes many Australian cycads prized by collectors of rare plants and by gardeners. Discover the species and how to grow them.
The genus Microcycas: one species, Microcycas calocoma, a Critically Endangered cycad from western Cuba. Learn about its biology, conservation and care.
The genus Stangeria: Stangeria eriopus, a fern-like cycad from South Africa and Mozambique first described as a fern. Discover its traits and cultivation.
The genus Zamia: about 80 New World cycads from Florida to Bolivia, including the only epiphytic cycad. Hardiness, cultivation, propagation and species.
Family Didiereaceae: the spiny trees of Madagascar plus Portulacaria and Calyptrotheca of Africa. Discover its taxonomy, ecology, genera and conservation.
The genus Alluaudia: six spiny, semi-succulent trees endemic to the spiny forest of Madagascar, family Didiereaceae. Species, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Alluaudiopsis: two rare spiny shrubs of southwestern Madagascar, family Didiereaceae. Discover species, ecology, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Decaryia: Decaryia madagascariensis, a zigzag-branched spiny shrub of Madagascar, family Didiereaceae. Its biology, cultivation and conservation.
The genus Didierea: the two octopus trees of the Madagascar spiny forest, type genus of Didiereaceae. Morphology, species, cultivation and conservation.
Family Dioscoreaceae: yams, caudiciform succulents and bat flowers across four genera, Dioscorea, Tacca, Trichopus and Stenomeris. Taxonomy and ecology.
The genus Dioscorea: staple yams and caudiciform elephant's-foot succulents, family Dioscoreaceae. Explore its biology, species, cultivation and status.
Family Euphorbiaceae: the spurge family, from Euphorbia and Jatropha to rubber, cassava and castor oil. Explore its classification, subfamilies and latex.
The genus Euphorbia: about 2,000 species, some 500 of them succulent, in four subgenera. Discover the cyathium, sections, growth forms and distribution.
Family Fouquieriaceae: the ocotillo family, one genus Fouquieria with eleven North American species, including the boojum tree. Taxonomy, ecology, species.
The genus Fouquieria: eleven desert species of North America, including the ocotillo and the boojum tree, family Fouquieriaceae. Ecology, species and care.
The Malvaceae family: about 4,200 species, from hibiscus, cotton and cacao to the pachycaul baobabs of the genus Adansonia. Traits, uses and conservation.
The Moringaceae family: one genus, Moringa, with 13 species, from the miracle tree Moringa oleifera to the bottle trees of Namibia and Madagascar.
The Pedaliaceae family: sesame and the pachycaul genera Uncarina and Pterodiscus, prized by succulent collectors. Traits, distribution and economic uses.
Encyclopedia of ornamental plants: succulents, palms, cycads, bamboos, aquatic plants. Clear, reliable growing guides, even for beginners.
The Vitaceae family: the grapevine family of about 900 species, including Cyphostemma, pachycaul succulents of Africa and Madagascar. Ecology and uses.
